headline: Phoenix Girl's Diaper Drive Collects 30,000 Donations in Four Years
meta_description: At age 8, Sloan noticed empty shelves at a food bank and launched a donation drive. Her fifth annual collection brought nearly 30,000 diapers to Nourish Phoeni…
summary_short: What started as one child's response to bare shelves at a food bank has grown into a sustained effort delivering tens of thousands of diapers to families in need.
body:
At age 8, Sloan from Phoenix noticed empty diaper shelves at a food bank and decided to act. Rather than let the observation fade, she started a donation drive to fill that gap.

Four years of commitment followed. Her fifth annual drive collected nearly 30,000 diapers for Nourish Phoenix—enough to restock shelves that serve the community's most vulnerable families. What began as one child's simple idea has become a reliable source of support for an organization working to address food insecurity and basic needs.

Sloan's sustained effort shows how persistent, direct action by one person can compound into meaningful impact. By returning to the same need year after year, she transformed a moment of concern into lasting change.
quick_facts: Sloan started the drive at age 8 in Phoenix
Donations went to Nourish Phoenix food bank
Four-year span from first observation to major impact
